requirement: FastAPI POST /telemetry/bulk endpoint inserting batches of readings using SQLAlchemy 2.0 multi-row insert with .returning() in strictly 1 INSERT statement per 50-row batch, committing generated IDs.
skeleton: FastAPI POST /telemetry/bulk with SQLAlchemy bulk multi-row insert and returning.
caption: A FastAPI ingestion endpoint that inserts a batch of telemetry rows with one multi-row INSERT and echoes the generated ids. The module builds a StaticPool engine over in-memory SQLite and a QueryCounter with class-level insert_count and statements, fed by a before_cursor_execute listener registered through SQLAlchemy's event API that counts statements beginning with INSERT. TelemetryReading under a DeclarativeBase has an autoincrement id, device_id, metric_name, a float value, and a string timestamp. get_db yields a session per request and closes it in finally; reset_db drops and recreates the schema and resets the counter, and runs at import. pydantic models TelemetryReadingCreate, BulkTelemetryRequest holding a readings list, and BulkTelemetryResponse with inserted_count and ids frame the API. GET /query-metrics returns the insert count and GET /telemetry returns the row total through func.count. POST /telemetry/bulk declares status 201 and BulkTelemetryResponse: it raises HTTPException 400 with detail Readings payload cannot be empty when the list is empty, dumps every reading to a dict, builds insert(TelemetryReading).returning(TelemetryReading.id), executes that statement once with the whole list of parameter dicts so SQLAlchemy 2.0 renders one INSERT with many VALUES rows, collects the returned ids in order, commits, and returns the count with the id list. A fifty-row batch therefore increments the insert counter exactly once, persists all fifty rows, and answers with fifty ids running from the first generated id to the last.

rationale.teaches: A SQLAlchemy 2.0 multi-row insert with returning: one INSERT per batch, a commit, a rejected empty payload, every row included, and the generated ids echoed back.
rationale.why: A per-row loop returns the same ids as a bulk insert, so only a statement count separates them. The family makes the statement count and the id echo part of the contract a generator must meet.

candidates.why_wrong: Each reading is inserted with its own statement, so a 50-row batch issues 50 INSERTs instead of one.
The batch is flushed but never committed, so the rows disappear when the session closes.
An empty readings list is accepted and answered 200 instead of rejected with 400.
The last reading in every batch is sliced off before insert, so each batch persists one row short.
returning is dropped, so the response reports a count but an empty ids list.
